subject.title: [Feature]: When messages are merged and processed, the agent event is expected to carry the original runId(s)

question: Should merged queued Gateway agent/chat events preserve the executed run ID and add an additive original/source run ID array, or should merged execution reuse one of the source run IDs as the public run ID?
rationale: Current code tracks enough queue lifecycle internally to explain the gap, but choosing public event semantics changes a stable Gateway API contract and should be a maintainer decision.

options.title: Add additive lineage array
options.body: Preserve the executed `runId` and add a named array such as `sourceRunIds` or `originalRunIds` to public schemas and projections.

options.title: Reuse one source run ID
options.body: Make merged execution appear under the first or last queued source ID, which helps simple clients but hides multi-source lineage and changes run identity semantics.

options.title: Keep singular contract
options.body: Leave clients to correlate through final events and session/history data, accepting that merged queued execution is not one-to-one in live events.

recommendation.title: Add additive lineage array
recommendation.body: Preserve the executed `runId` and add a named array such as `sourceRunIds` or `originalRunIds` to public schemas and projections.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest recent owner signal for the current Gateway event projection surface and public API landing decisions in this area.
